caveats: Summaries and sentences are verbatim (whitespace-normalised) NASA text; key_sentences were selected by LANDFALL using the shipped anchors, the wording is NASA's.
Educational web pages, not standards: no thresholds or requirement IDs come from this snapshot.

Distance hazard page says a Mars communication delay of 'up to 20 minutes one way' (HRP's rounded general-audience figure). This snapshot carries no other light-time number; computed Earth-Mars light times must come from their own source (e.g. JPL Horizons) - do not mix the two in one claim.

data.lede: Astronauts encounter five hazards as they journey through space. Recognizing these hazards allows NASA to seek ways that overcome the challenges of sending humans to the space station, the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

hazards.name: Space Radiation
hazards.summary: Invisible to the human eye, space radiation is not only stealthy but considered one of the most hazardous aspects of spaceflight.

page.title: Hazard: Space Radiation
page.lede: Space radiation is invisible to the human eye. It’s not only stealthy, but considered one of the most hazardous aspects of human spaceflight.

key_sentences.sentence: Radiation exposure increases cancer risk, damages the central nervous system, can alter cognitive function, reduce motor function, and prompt behavioral changes.

hazards.name: Isolation and Confinement
hazards.summary: Behavioral responses occur among groups of people far from Earth who are isolated and confined in a small space over a long period of time.

page.title: Hazard: Isolation and Confinement
page.lede: Behavioral responses occur among groups of people far from Earth who are isolated and confined in a small space over a long period of time. Crews will be carefully chosen, trained, and supported to ensure they can work effectively as a team for months or years in space.

key_sentences.anchor: Sleep loss, circadian desynchronization, and work overload
key_sentences.sentence: Sleep loss, circadian desynchronization, and work overload compound this issue and may lead to decreased performance, adverse health outcomes, and compromised mission objectives.
Research is also being conducted in workload and performance, light therapy for circadian alignment, phase shifting and alertness.

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.summary: Instructions, new supplies, medical care, and more become increasingly challenging to receive from Earth as astronauts venture deeper into space.

page.title: Hazard: Distance From Earth
page.lede: Instructions, new supplies, medical care, and more become increasingly challenging to receive from Earth as astronauts venture deeper into space.

key_sentences.anchor: communication delay of up to 20 minutes one way
key_sentences.sentence: Facing a communication delay of up to 20 minutes one way, the possibility of equipment failures or medical emergencies, and a critical need to ration food and supplies, astronauts must be capable of confronting an array of situations with minimal support from teams on Earth.

hazards.name: Gravity Fields
hazards.summary: Astronauts' entire bodies – muscles, bones, inner ear, and organs – must adjust to the new gravities encountered on the space station or their spacecraft, as well as on the Moon, Mars, and Earth once they return home.

page.title: Hazard: Gravity Fields
page.lede: Floating weightlessly within a spacecraft can lead to dizziness, bone and muscle loss, vision issues, and more. Astronauts may also need time to adjust to new gravity fields after landing on the Moon or Mars before they conduct mission-critical tasks. Developing strategies that enable crew members to adapt quickly to different gravitational fields will be key to mission success.

key_sentences.anchor: lose on average 1% to 1.5% of mineral density per month
key_sentences.sentence: Without the continuous load of Earth’s gravity, weight-bearing bones lose on average 1% to 1.5% of mineral density per month during spaceflight.

key_sentences.anchor: increased risk of developing kidney stones
key_sentences.sentence: If preventive measures are not implemented, crews may experience an increased risk of developing kidney stones due to dehydration and increased excretion of calcium from their bones.

hazards.name: Hostile/Closed Environments
hazards.summary: Maintaining a safe ecosystem inside a spacecraft presents unique challenges, from ensuring optimal temperatures, pressures, and lighting, to reducing noise, monitoring microbial communities, and tracking immune responses.

page.title: Hazard: Hostile/Closed Environments
page.lede: Maintaining a safe ecosystem inside a vehicle presents unique challenges, from ensuring optimal temperatures, pressures, and lighting, to reducing noise, monitoring microbial communities, and tracking immune responses.

key_sentences.sentence: Stress hormone levels can elevate and the immune system can alter, which could lead to increased susceptibility to allergies or other illnesses.
